question.prompt:
An array of numbers is constructed beginning with the numbers \(-1,\) \(3,\) \(1\) in the top row. Each adjacent pair of numbers is summed to produce a number in the next row. Each row will begin and end with the numbers \(-1\) and \(1,\) respectively. The first three rows are shown below.

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_10A_Q19_question_fig1.svg)

If the process continues, one of the rows will sum to \(12{,}288.\) In that row, what is the third number from the left?

solutions.explanation:
We can track the row sum and the requested entry without constructing the rest of the array. Number the top row as row \(0\), so row \(n\) is reached after \(n\) transitions.

Each interior entry contributes to two adjacent-pair sums in the next row. Each endpoint contributes to one adjacent-pair sum and also reappears as an endpoint. Thus every old entry is counted twice in the new row sum. The initial sum is \(-1+3+1=3\), so row \(n\) has sum
\[
S_n=3\cdot2^n.
\]
Since
\[
12{,}288=3\cdot4096=3\cdot2^{12},
\]
the desired row is reached after \(12\) transitions. These positive sums double each time, so this row is unique.

Let \(b_j\) and \(c_j\) be the second and third entries after \(j\) transitions. The first entry stays \(-1\), so the second entry decreases by \(1\) each time:
\[
b_0=3,
\qquad b_{j+1}=b_j-1,
\qquad b_j=3-j.
\]
The next third entry is the sum of the current second and third entries. Thus \(c_{j+1}=c_j+b_j\), starting with \(c_0=1\).

To reach row \(12\), we therefore add the twelve second entries from rows \(0\) through \(11\), namely \(3,2,1,0,-1,\ldots,-8\). Pairing the first with the last, the second with the next-to-last, and so on gives six pairs, each summing to \(-5\). Hence
\[
c_{12}=1+6(-5)=\boxed{-29},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutions.title: Track the row sum and the first three entries

solutions.explanation:
View each entry as a sum of contributions from the three starting numbers. At each transition, an entry sends one copy of its value to the same numbered position and another copy one position to the right. Adding the copies that arrive at each position reproduces the adjacent-pair rule, including the endpoints.

Every value is copied twice, so the row sum doubles. Starting from sum \(3\), the sum after \(n\) transitions is \(3\cdot2^n\). Because
\[
12{,}288=3\cdot2^{12},
\]
the required row is reached after exactly \(12\) transitions.

A contribution's route is determined by choosing, at each transition, whether it stays in the same numbered position or moves one position right. To end in the third position after twelve transitions:

From the first starting position, a contribution must move right exactly twice. Choose the two transition numbers in \(12\cdot11\) ordered ways, then divide by \(2\), since each pair was counted in both orders. There are \(66\) routes, each carrying the starting value \(-1\).

From the second starting position, a contribution must move right exactly once. There are \(12\) choices of transition, each carrying the starting value \(3\).

From the third starting position, it must never move right. There is one route, carrying the starting value \(1\).

These cases include every contribution, since each originates at one of the three starting positions. Each route is counted once by its set of right-moving transitions; a route with too many right moves cannot return to the third position. Therefore the third entry is
\[
(-1)(66)+3(12)+1=\boxed{-29},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutions.title: Count contributions from the starting numbers
